chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
Beware that destitution is a calamity, but worse than destitution is the ailment of the body, and worse than the ailment of the body is the disease of the heart.
ai.seo_question: What is the hierarchy of calamities according to Imam Ali in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) delineates a spiritual hierarchy of afflictions, progressing from material poverty (faqr) to physical illness, and culminating in the spiritual disease of the heart (marad al-qalb). In Shia scholarly tradition, this 'disease of the heart'—often interpreted as doubt, hypocrisy, or spiritual blindness—is considered the most severe because it corrupts the soul's connection to the Divine, rendering it more critical than bodily suffering. This triad underscores the holistic Islamic view of well-being, where spiritual integrity is paramount over material or physical comfort.
